cells.tense: You are moving first and drawing the line, right here where you stand, and you know it.
cells.ask: offer one moment of not knowing out loud, today
cells.core:
You can decide and you can hold at the same time. You say what will happen, and then you carry it while it happens. The strength isn't separate from the choosing — it's what makes the choosing stand. This is what it looks like when it's going well: a line drawn clean and a body that can keep standing behind it.

There is a quieter thing this is ready to feed, and it isn't more force. It's curiosity. You don't have to have the answer before you move; you can move and find out. The carrying gets lighter when the certainty gets looser. That returns a strength that learns while it holds. The weight is still there. It lands differently when it's said out loud, though.
cells.sheetLine: You decide and you carry it, and you're allowed to not know one thing today.

cells.tense: Ahead of you is a weight nobody has handed you yet, and you are already bracing under it.
cells.ask: let one thing stay unexplained and let what the facts actually say do the understanding
cells.core:
You can decide and you can hold when it's called for. You say what will happen, and then you carry it while it happens; the strength isn't separate from the choosing. This is what it looks like when it's going well: a line drawn where it's needed and a body sturdy enough to hold it.

But the bracing has jumped ahead of the load. You defend a line before anyone has crossed it, prepare for the heaviest version, live at a finish line only you can see. Rushing the future costs the body meant to carry the present. There is a different move, and it isn't more force. Step back and read what is actually in front of you. Understanding arrives on its own when you stop pushing it. That is what your strength has been waiting on.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying weight that hasn't arrived yet, and it's taking the strength you have now.
cells.verb: setting the boundary and stepping first
cells.place: the part of you that carries weight without breaking

cells.tense: Behind you is a boundary you once set, and you are still standing at its door as if it were ahead.
cells.ask: make one overdue structural change slowly, and let the falling be enough
cells.core:
You can decide and you can hold when it's called for. You say what will happen, and then you carry it while it happens; the strength isn't separate from the choosing. This is what it looks like when it's going well: a line drawn where it's needed, and a body that can stand behind it for as long as it takes.

But the deciding quit a while back, and the holding went flat. You are still bearing weight — you're just not choosing anymore. The line went undrawn. More effort won't do it, and feeling your way back won't either. One structure that's overdue needs to fall, and you let it fall. Not fast. Not clean. Just persistent. Ground that you actually chose comes back under you.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped deciding and kept carrying, and the carrying has no direction without you.

cells.tense: Most days you draw the line, and the room shapes itself around it — while the story you tell is that you only kept the peace.
cells.ask: name one boundary you have already drawn and admit you are the one who drew it
cells.core:
You can decide and you can hold when it's called for. You say what will happen, and then you carry it while it happens; the strength isn't separate from the choosing. This is what it looks like when it's going well: a line drawn where it's needed, a body steady behind it, and things that make sense in your presence.

The choosing is already running. You set the terms, you draw the line, you decide what gets carried and what gets let go. And somehow the account comes out as if the weight decided for itself. That decision is in your hands. You just haven't claimed it. Nothing new needs deciding. Try saying out loud that you are the one who decided. A strength that knows its own name comes back.
cells.sheetLine: You're already steering this. You've just been calling it carrying.
